title: Plankton: Reconciling Binary Code and Debug Information
problem: Existing binary lifters produce insufficiently precise intermediate representations for rigorous static analysis, while traditional compilation-based approaches require intrusive interference with the build system.
motivation: Static analysis is essential for large-scale software defect detection, but current binary-based approaches lack the precision needed for practical deployment.
method: Plankton reads debug information (metadata like variable names and types) that compilers embed in binaries. It uses two reconciliation algorithms to identify and fix mismatches between what the compiled code shows and what the debug information claims, making them consistent. This produces clean LLVM intermediate representations (the standard format analysis tools use), which enables thorough static analysis of binaries without any changes to the build process.
key_novelty: The core innovation is using debug metadata combined with reconciliation algorithms to precisely lift binaries (translate them into analysis-ready code) without modifying the build system.
contributions: Plankton: a binary lifter producing high-quality LLVM IRs from binaries with debug information
Two novel algorithms for reconciling low-level and high-level code representations
Demonstrated static analysis results achieving 82.8% agreement with compilation-based approaches
76.9% improvement in analysis precision over existing binary lifters

metrics.accuracy: 17.2% difference from compilation-based approach; 76.9% improvement over existing lifters

primary_theme: Binary code lifting for practical static analysis
